clue.text: Ancient invader offers perspective

definitions.meaning: a member of the Germanic people who settled in England after the Romans left
a point of view or way of looking at something

explanation.surface: A historical raider is said to give us a new point of view.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angles invaded Britain in the fifth century; a slant or viewpoint on a subject is also called this.

clue.text: Beast runs right round a German river

indicators.note: the two single letters stand around the remaining pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
ein is German for a
the Dee is a river in Britain

explanation.surface: An animal stampedes along the bank of a German river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' wraps the two R letters (runs, right) around the German and the river; Britain's Dee is a common crossword river.
explanation.definitionFit: A reindeer is an animal, the Arctic deer that pulls sleighs.

clue.text: Battered chest containing yard tool

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the next piece inside them
something battered is knocked out of shape, so the letters of chest are rearranged

explanation.surface: A beaten-up box in the garden holds a gardening implement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battered' rearranges CHEST into SCTHE; 'containing' puts Y inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A scythe is a long-bladed implement for cutting grass or crops.

clue.text: Bishop has spoiled party

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: something spoiled is ruined or messed up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A clergyman has ruined the celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoiled' rearranges HAS into ASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Bash is informal slang for a lively party or celebration.

clue.text: One-dimensional Shakespearean king stays home

indicators.note: the king stays with home inside him, holding that piece within

parts.note: King Lear is the title character of a Shakespeare tragedy
in means at home

explanation.surface: A flat Shakespearean monarch who never leaves the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stays' reads as the king staying at home: the king holds the word for home.
explanation.definitionFit: Something linear runs along a single line, so it has only length as its measure.

clue.text: Task and chore to mix something to eat

indicators.note: to mix is to stir together, so the letters of both words are combined and rearranged

explanation.surface: A kitchen chore: mixing up something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to mix' rearranges TASK and CHORE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortcake is a crumbly biscuit or cake, so it is a food.

clue.text: Paint Dean Court ground

indicators.note: ground is crushed or milled, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Painting the grounds of a building called Dean Court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a noun for the court's land but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Undercoat is the base layer of coating applied before the final topcoat.

clue.text: Mean to get wasted

definitions.meaning: stingy or reluctant to spend money

explanation.surface: A miser deciding to get drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight means both miserly with money and, informally, intoxicated.

clue.text: African transmitter sets in hollow tree

indicators.note: the first word goes inside what is left of the hollowed word
a hollow tree has had its insides removed, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: Something from Africa lodges in a hollow tree trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow' leaves T and E of TREE; SETS goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse fly of Africa transmits sleeping sickness, so it is a disease carrier.

clue.text: Way to load part-emptied revolver?

indicators.note: the remaining letters are loaded with the other piece, holding it inside
the word part is emptied of its middle letters, leaving its ends

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road or way

explanation.surface: A method of loading a partly empty gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emptied' keeps only the ends of 'part'; 'to load' fills them with the way. 'revolver' suggests a pistol, but a planet revolves round the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A planet circles its star, so it is playfully a revolver; the question mark flags this whimsical sense.

clue.text: Drunk shortly drinking last of booze in pub

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take in the next piece, swallowing it inside
someone drunk staggers about, so these letters are jumbled
only the final letter of booze is taken

explanation.surface: A tipsy man soon downing the last of his drink in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' rearranges SHORTLY into HOSTLRY; 'drinking' puts E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostelry is an old-fashioned or humorous word for an inn or tavern.

clue.text: Wingers of value in one Madrid team for show

indicators.note: those two letters go inside the next piece

parts.note: Real Madrid is a Spanish football club

indicators.note: the wingers are the outside letters of value, its first and last

explanation.surface: A football club's wide players showing their worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wingers of' takes V and E from VALUE; 'in' places them inside REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal something is to display or uncover it, so show is a synonym.

clue.text: Animal in lake with Buddhist monk

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk

explanation.surface: A creature beside a lake with a monk from Tibet.
explanation.definitionFit: A llama is a South American beast of burden related to the camel.

clue.text: Again and again?

parts.note: doing something once and then again makes two times; one more 'again' makes three times

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about repetition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Again and again' reads as 'repeatedly', but taken literally an act done, then again, then again happens three times.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrice means three times, and an act repeated twice over occurs three times in all.

clue.text: Something done about meat supplied

indicators.note: the first piece goes about, or around, the next piece

parts.note: a deed is an act or something done
liver is offal eaten as meat

explanation.surface: A job done involving meat that was supplied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets the act around the meat; 'Something done' is a noun phrase, not the past tense it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Delivered means handed over or provided, as goods are supplied.

clue.text: Stick close to flatmate in block

indicators.note: that letter goes inside the next piece

parts.note: to bar is to block or obstruct

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so just its final letter is taken

explanation.surface: Keeping near a housemate in an apartment building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' gives E, the end of FLATMATE; 'in' puts it in BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick or bear something is to tolerate or put up with it.

clue.text: Good people achieving freedom from sin

parts.note: a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: Virtuous folk reaching a state of purity.
explanation.definitionFit: In Christian teaching, being in a state of grace means being spiritually pure and forgiven.

clue.text: Sort of music book extracted from rubbish

indicators.note: the letter is extracted, pulled out, from the longer word

parts.note: garbage is rubbish or trash

explanation.surface: A kind of music book pulled out of the rubbish bin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extracted from' removes B from GARBAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Garage is a genre of electronic dance music, named after a New York club.

clue.text: Fish convulse when beheaded

indicators.note: a beheaded word loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: to shake is to convulse or tremble

explanation.surface: A fish thrashes in spasms when its head is cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when beheaded' drops S from SHAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hake is a sea fish of the cod family, common on menus.

clue.text: Carriage said to be well-proportioned

indicators.note: said signals that the word is spoken, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: a hansom is a two-wheeled horse-drawn cab

explanation.surface: A horse-drawn coach is reputedly elegantly shaped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' gives a word sounding like HANSOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome can mean nicely shaped or of pleasing form, as in a handsome building.

clue.text: Spend colder months in Kraków in terror

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Passing the cold season in a Polish city in fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points inside KRAKÓW IN TERROR, where the letters run from 'in' into 'terror'.
explanation.definitionFit: To winter somewhere is to pass the cold season there, as birds or holidaymakers do.

clue.text: Beer fuels explosive ability

indicators.note: the drink fuels the explosive by being put inside it

parts.note: TNT is the explosive trinitrotoluene
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Drink feeds an explosive gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fuels' puts the beer inside the explosive, which is its abbreviation rather than a describing word.
explanation.definitionFit: Talent is a natural aptitude or skill, so it is a synonym for ability.

clue.text: Have riches perhaps in American vault

parts.note: to bound is to leap or vault

explanation.surface: Perhaps there is wealth in a bank vault in the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vault' suggests a strongroom of riches but is the verb, to jump.
explanation.definitionFit: To abound is to be plentiful, so a place may abound in riches; 'perhaps' marks riches as one example.

clue.text: Delphic priestess in wicker boat seen topless

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, which goes

parts.note: a coracle is a small round boat of wicker covered in hide

explanation.surface: A Greek priestess seen bare-chested in a basket boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes C from CORACLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pythia at Delphi was a prophetess consulted on the future; she was the famous Greek seer.

clue.text: EU collecting money raised forms alliance

indicators.note: in a down entry raising reads the whole thing from bottom to top
the letters of EU collect the next piece, holding it between them

parts.note: tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: The European Union gathers funds to form a coalition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collecting' puts the money inside EU, giving ETINU; 'raised' reads that upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to join together, as parties do when making a coalition.

clue.text: Excited seeing leg — not small — in flimsy robe

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Seeing a bare leg causes a stir in someone wearing a sheer robe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not small' takes S out of SEEING LEG; 'Excited' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A negligee is a light, often sheer, dressing gown worn by women.

clue.text: Takes in tea brewed by son

indicators.note: brewed tea is stewed, so its letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A son has made a pot of tea and drinks it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' rearranges TEA into EAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat food is to consume it, taking it into the body.

clue.text: Sailor posted away

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
sent means posted, as a letter

explanation.surface: A seaman has been dispatched elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent means not present, gone from a place.

clue.text: Creature in riotous binge

indicators.note: riotous means wild and disorderly, so the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: An animal caught up in a wild drinking bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word; 'riotous' rearranges BINGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A being is any living thing, a synonym for creature.

clue.text: Hardened companion comes to standstill

parts.note: stale bread has hardened
a mate is a friend or companion

explanation.surface: A tough partner grinds to a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalemate is a deadlock where neither side can make progress, from the chess term.
